effects: The signer pays exactly reservationFee in native SGB (msg.value must equal it), which goes to reservationFeeRecipient, an address read from storage.
A new minting-tag NFT (id = nextAvailableTag) is minted to the signer with _safeMint.
The new tag's minting recipient is set to the signer and its executor is cleared (_afterTokenTransfer).
formats.shown: Intent 'reserve minting tag' with the native value paid shown as 'Reservation Fee' in SGB.

findings.title: reserve: the fee recipient and the new tag id come from storage and are not shown.
findings.evidence: MintingTagManager.sol reserve(): Transfers.transferNAT(reservationFeeRecipient, msg.value); _reserve uses nextAvailableTag. The descriptor shows only @.value 'Reservation Fee'.
findings.fix: None possible from calldata. You could add 'to the Flare fee recipient' to the intent.

findings.title: reserve test sends 1 SGB, but the deployed initial fee is 1000 SGB and must match exactly.
findings.evidence: cases/0.json value 1000000000000000000. meta.json constructor _reservationFee 1000000000000000000000. reserve(): require(msg.value == reservationFee). Governance may have changed the fee since.
findings.fix: Use the current on-chain reservationFee in the test value.

effects: Only the tag owner can call this. It changes the address that receives FXRP minted with this tag to _recipient, which must be non-zero.
formats.shown: Intent 'set mint recipient' with the Tag Id and the new Recipient address.

findings.title: setMintingRecipient: recipient address types eoa/wallet are narrower than the code allows.
findings.evidence: descriptor: #._recipient params.types ['eoa','wallet']. MintingTagManager.setMintingRecipient only requires _recipient != address(0), so a contract is valid.
findings.fix: Add 'contract' to types, or drop the types restriction.

effects: Only the tag owner can call this. It schedules _executor as the only address allowed to execute direct mintings with the tag, active after executorChangeAfterSeconds (from storage). Until then the old executor stays active.
If a change is pending and _executor equals the currently active executor, the pending change is cancelled instead.
Zero address means anyone may execute.
formats.shown: Intent 'Set mint executor (delayed)' with the Tag Id and the executor address, labelled 'zero = anyone'.

findings.title: setAllowedExecutor: the delay length and the cancel-pending behaviour are not shown.
findings.evidence: _setExecutor: allowedExecutorActiveAfterTs = block.timestamp + executorChangeAfterSeconds (storage). When changePending && _executor == currentAllowedExecutor it emits AllowedExecutorChangeCancelled. The intent says only '(delayed)'.
findings.fix: None needed beyond the intent. The delay is a storage value.

effects: The signer's minting-tag NFT moves to _to (ERC721 _transfer, which requires the signer to be the owner; it is not a safe transfer).
The tag's minting recipient is reset to _to.
Any allowed executor, old or pending, is cleared immediately.
formats.shown: Intent 'Transfer minting tag, reset settings' with the To address and the Tag Id.

findings.title: transfer: 'reset settings' does not say that the recipient becomes the new owner and the executor is cleared.
findings.fix: Intent such as 'Transfer minting tag (mint recipient set to new owner, executor cleared)'.

findings.title: transfer: 'To' address types eoa/wallet are narrower than the code allows.
findings.evidence: descriptor: #._to params.types ['eoa','wallet']. transfer() calls ERC721 _transfer, which accepts any non-zero address, including contracts.
findings.fix: Add 'contract' to types, or drop the types restriction.
